answer_text:
# 🥛 Calcium-Containing Foods

Calcium is the most abundant mineral in your body and a major component of your bones and teeth. Since your body can't make calcium on its own, it's essential to consume calcium-rich foods to meet your daily needs.

Calcium is used for numerous functions, including building bones and teeth, muscle contraction, blood clotting, maintenance of cell membranes, and nerve transmission.

---

## 🧀 Dairy Products (Highest Sources)

Dairy products (milk, cheese, yogurt, etc.) are the most concentrated food sources of calcium — for example, one cup of milk contains approximately 271 mg of calcium.

| Food | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Milk** | One of the richest sources of calcium |
| **Yogurt** | Also rich in probiotics |
| **Cheese (Parmesan)** | Highest among cheeses |
| **Cheese (others)** | Swiss, cheddar, brie, etc. |

Yogurt is an excellent source of calcium, and many types are also rich in probiotics — a type of beneficial bacteria that can promote immune function, improve heart health, and enhance nutrient absorption.

Most cheeses are excellent sources of calcium. Parmesan cheese has the most, with 242 mg — or 24% of the Daily Value — per ounce (28 grams).

---

## 🐟 Fish & Seafood

Sardines and canned salmon are loaded with calcium, thanks to their edible bones.

| Food | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Sardines (canned)** | Edible bones = high calcium |
| **Salmon (canned, pink)** | ~241 mg per 3 oz |

---

## 🌿 Plant-Based Sources

Many plant foods are also calcium-rich, including greens, beans, tofu, nuts, and seeds.

| Food | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Tofu** | Most concentrated non-dairy calcium source |
| **Kale & Bok Choy** | Better absorbed than spinach |
| **Broccoli** | Good bioavailability |
| **White beans / Black beans** | ~239 mg per cup (raw) |
| **Turnip greens** | ~209 mg per cup (cooked) |
| **Almonds** | Healthy snack with calcium |
| **Sesame seeds / Chia seeds / Poppy seeds** | High in calcium |

Tofu is the most concentrated source of non-dairy calcium.

Seeds are tiny nutritional powerhouses, and many are high in calcium, including poppy, sesame, celery, and chia seeds.

The bioavailability of calcium from plants that do not contain oxalic acid — including broccoli, kale, and cabbage — is similar to that of milk, although the amount of calcium per serving is much lower.

---

## 🥣 Fortified Foods

Fortified foods like cereals can make it easier to meet your daily calcium needs.

You can also find a variety of plant-based beverages, such as plant milks and orange juice, that have been fortified with calcium.

---

## ⚠️ Important Tips

- Vitamin D is required for calcium to be absorbed in the gut and to maintain adequate calcium levels in the blood.
- Certain compounds in plants (e.g., oxalic acid, phytic acid) can decrease calcium absorption by forming indigestible salts with calcium.
- Your body absorbs the calcium in dairy products more easily than that from plant sources.
- The recommended dietary allowance for calcium ranges from **1,000 to 1,200 mg for adults**, depending on age.

Eating a **variety** of calcium-rich foods from both dairy and plant-based sources is the best strategy to meet your daily calcium needs! 💪
